title: US State Privacy Laws Security Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to comply with US state privacy laws including Texas, Virginia, Colorado. Protect your data with actionable steps.
intro: Navigate the complex landscape of US state privacy laws with this comprehensive checklist. From Texas DPRA to Virginia CDPA and Colorado CPA, ensure your personal data is protected under evolving state regulations.

sections.title: Understanding Your Rights Under State Laws

items.task: Identify which state privacy laws apply to you
items.why: Different states have varying privacy protections and requirements that may affect your data rights.
items.howTo: Review your state's privacy laws (California CCPA, Virginia CDPA, Colorado CPA, Texas DPRA, Connecticut CTDPA). Check if you're covered as a resident or if businesses you interact with must comply.

items.why: State laws grant specific rights like data deletion, correction, and opt-out that you can exercise.
items.howTo: Familiarize yourself with rights to access, delete, correct, and port your data. Understand opt-out rights for data sales and targeted advertising. Keep a list of these rights for reference.

items.task: Understand what constitutes sensitive personal information
items.why: State laws provide enhanced protections for sensitive data categories requiring explicit consent.
items.howTo: Learn that sensitive data includes racial origin, religious beliefs, health information, biometrics, geolocation, and sexual orientation. Review what data categories you share online.

items.task: Audit your current data sharing practices
items.why: Understanding what personal information you're sharing helps you make informed privacy decisions.
items.howTo: Review privacy settings on social media, shopping accounts, and apps. List companies that have your data. Check what information you've provided to employers, healthcare providers, and financial institutions.

items.task: Request data access reports from major companies
items.why: Accessing your data helps you understand what information companies collect and how they use it.
items.howTo: Submit data access requests to major platforms like Google, Facebook, Amazon, and data brokers. Use company privacy portals or email privacy contacts. Keep records of requests and responses.

items.task: Opt out of data sales and sharing
items.why: State laws allow you to prevent companies from selling your personal information to third parties.
items.howTo: Look for 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' links on websites. Submit opt-out requests to data brokers. Use Incognito Browser to prevent tracking when researching opt-out procedures.

items.why: Reduces profiling and limits how your data is used for advertising purposes across platforms.
items.howTo: Disable targeted ads in Google, Facebook, and other platforms. Use ad preference centers to limit data use. Enable 'Limit Ad Tracking' on mobile devices and browsers.

items.task: Stay updated on privacy policy changes
items.why: Companies regularly update privacy practices, and state laws require notification of material changes.
items.howTo: Set up alerts for privacy policy updates from companies you use. Review annual privacy reports. Subscribe to privacy news sources to stay informed about new state law requirements.

items.task: Keep records of privacy requests and responses
items.why: Documentation helps track compliance and provides evidence if you need to file complaints with state authorities.
items.howTo: Create a folder for privacy correspondence. Save emails, confirmation numbers, and response letters. Note dates of requests and company response times for future reference.

items.why: Technical tools help enforce your privacy preferences and reduce data collection automatically.
items.howTo: Use Incognito Browser for private browsing without tracking. Enable Global Privacy Control (GPC) to automatically signal opt-out preferences. Use VPNs and privacy-focused search engines.

items.task: Know how to file complaints for privacy violations
items.why: State attorneys general enforce privacy laws and can take action against non-compliant companies.
items.howTo: Locate your state's attorney general privacy complaint portal. Document any privacy violations or non-responsive companies. Understand the complaint process and required information.
